correctness.rationale: If h,k are persistent nonempty intersection lengths, fixed witness integers x,y add to a persistent witness for h+k, proving the positive failure-length set closed under addition; h=1 excluded by empty core. Every nonzero additive submonoid S of N0 is finitely generated using its least m and attained least elements in the m residue classes. Repeating each generator d infinitely often, define G_{j+1}=b_jG_j with increasing integer b_j>(D-1)h on sufficiently late tail, and A_q={G_j,-(d(j)-1)G_j:j>=q}. Sets decrease strictly; any persistent h-sum must be divisible by each G_q, hence must be 0. For fixed h, a zero sum with least nonzero block coefficient z_j obeys 0<|z_j|<b_j, yet zero modulo G_{j+1} forces b_j|z_j, impossible; hence all blocks separately balance and h lies in S. Conversely balanced pairs realize every h in S in every tail. S={0} handled by positive tails. Finite independent check S=<3,5>, h=1..8 agrees; this does not prove all q,h.
